الوصف
ما هو Perl؟

ما مدى استقرار Perl؟

متى لا يجب أن أبرمج بلغة Perl؟
ما الفرق بين "perl" و "Perl"؟
ما هو JAPH؟

perldebguts - Internal details of Perl debugger

NAME
perldebguts - Internal details of the Perl debugger
SYNOPSIS
DESCRIPTION
Internal Debugger API
The debugger is not a single module, but a collection of subs defined in various parts of the Perl core. This document attempts to give an overview of the debugger's internals.
Debugging Subroutines
The debugger subs can be found in the following files:
Accessing the Debugger API
To use the debugger API, you need to use the Perl API for calling Perl subroutines. The debugger subs are not exported by default.
DB<0xC2><0x80><0x8B>sub name
Returns the name of the subroutine.
DB<0xC2><0x80><0x8B>sub_line file, line
Returns the line number of the subroutine.
DB<0xC2><0x80><0x8B>sub_file file, line
Returns the file name of the subroutine.
DB<0xC2><0x80><0x8B>sub_args file, line
Returns the arguments of the subroutine.
DB<0xC2><0x80><0x8B>sub_returns file, line
Returns the return values of the subroutine.
DB<0xC2><0x80><0x8B>sub_exception file, line
Returns the exception thrown by the subroutine.
DB<0xC2><0x80><0x8B>sub_eval file, line
Evaluates the subroutine.
DB<0xC2><0x80><0x8B>sub_delete file, line
Deletes the subroutine.
DB<0xC2><0x80><0x8B>sub_list
Returns a list of all subroutines.
DB<0xC2><0x80><0x8B>sub_trace file, line
Traces the subroutine.

"-d:-foo", "-d:-foo=bar"
New C APIs

"\cX"

Perl 4-era .pl libraries

Devel::DProf
Performance Enhancements
"Safe signals" optimisation
Optimisation of shift() and pop() calls without arguments
Optimisation of regexp engine string comparison work
Regular expression compilation speed-up
String appending is 100 times faster
Eliminate "PL_*" accessor functions under ithreads
Freeing weak references
Lexical array and hash assignments
@_ uses less memory
Size optimisations to SV and HV structures
Memory consumption improvements to Exporter
Memory savings for weak references
"%+" and "%-" use less memory
Multiple small improvements to threads
Adjacent pairs of nextstate opcodes are now optimized away
Modules and Pragmata
New Modules and Pragmata
Updated Modules and Pragma
much less configuration dialog hassle, support for META/MYMETA.json, support for local::lib, support for HTTP::Tiny to reduce the dependency on FTP sites, automatic mirror selection, iron out all known bugs in configure_requires, support for distributions compressed with bzip2(1), allow Foo/Bar.pm on the command line to mean "Foo::Bar", charinfo(), charscript(), charblock()
Removed Modules and Pragmata
Documentation
New Documentation
Changes to Existing Documentation
Diagnostics
New Diagnostics
Closure prototype called, Insecure user-defined property %s, panic: gp_free failed to free glob pointer - something is repeatedly re-creating entries, Parsing code internal error (%s), refcnt: fd %d%s, Regexp modifier "/%c" may not appear twice, Regexp modifiers "/%c" and "/%c" are mutually exclusive, Using !~ with %s doesn't make sense, "\b{" is deprecated; use "\b\{" instead, "\B{" is deprecated; use "\B\{" instead, Operation "%s" returns its argument for .., Use of qw(...) as parentheses is deprecated

perl561delta - what's new for perl v5.6.1

DESCRIPTION

Summary of changes between 5.6.0 and 5.6.1

Security Issues
Core bug fixes
UNIVERSAL::isa(), Memory leaks, Numeric conversions, qw(a\\b), caller(), Bugs in regular expressions, "slurp" mode, Autovivification of symbolic references to special variables, Lexical warnings, Spurious warnings and errors, glob(), Tainting, sort(), #line directives, Subroutine prototypes, map(), Debugger, PERL5OPT, chop(), Unicode support, 64-bit support, Compiler, Lvalue subroutines, IO::Socket, File::Find, xsubpp, "no Module;", Tests
Core features
Configuration issues
Documentation
Bundled modules
B::Concise, File::Temp, Pod::LaTeX, Pod::Text::Overstrike, CGI, CPAN, Class::Struct, DB_File, Devel::Peek, File::Find, Getopt::Long, IO::Poll, IPC::Open3, Math::BigFloat, Math::Complex, Net::Ping, Opcode, Pod::Parser, Pod::Text, SDBM_File, Sys::Syslog, Tie::RefHash, Tie::SubstrHash
Platform-specific improvements
NCR MP-RAS, NonStop-UX
Core Enhancements
Interpreter cloning, threads, and concurrency
Lexically scoped warning categories
Unicode and UTF-8 support
Support for interpolating named characters
"our" declarations
Support for strings represented as a vector of ordinals
Improved Perl version numbering system
New syntax for declaring subroutine attributes
File and directory handles can be autovivified
open() with more than two arguments
64-bit support
Large file support
Long doubles
"more bits"
Enhanced support for sort() subroutines
"sort $coderef @foo" allowed
File globbing implemented internally
Support for CHECK blocks
POSIX character class syntax [: :] supported
Better pseudo-random number generator
Improved "qw//" operator
Better worst-case behavior of hashes
pack() format 'Z' supported
pack() format modifier '!' supported
pack() and unpack() support counted strings
Comments in pack() templates
Weak references
Binary numbers supported
Lvalue subroutines
Some arrows may be omitted in calls through references
Boolean assignment operators are legal lvalues
exists() is supported on subroutine names
exists() and delete() are supported on array elements
Pseudo-hashes work better
Automatic flushing of output buffers
Better diagnostics on meaningless filehandle operations
Where possible, buffered data discarded from duped input filehandle
eof() has the same old magic as <>
binmode() can be used to set :crlf and :raw modes
"-T" filetest recognizes UTF-8 encoded files as "text"
system(), backticks and pipe open now reflect exec() failure
Improved diagnostics
Diagnostics follow STDERR
More consistent close-on-exec behavior
syswrite() ease-of-use
Better syntax checks on parenthesized unary operators
Bit operators support full native integer width
Improved security features
More functional bareword prototype (*)
"require" and "do" may be overridden
$^X variables may now have names longer than one character
New variable $^C reflects "-c" switch
New variable $^V contains Perl version as a string
Optional Y2K warnings
Arrays now always interpolate into double-quoted strings
@- and @+ provide starting/ending offsets of regex submatches

قائمة الميزات التجريبية في Perl

الوصف
التجارب الحالية
الكلمات المفتاحية القابلة للإضافة، الأسماء المستعارة عبر المرجع، `use re 'strict';`، تعريف مرجع لمتغير، يوجد هدف `installhtml` في Makefile، (محدود) البحث الخلفي متغير الطول، خطافات أحرف الاستخدام الخاص لليونيكود، أحرف البدل لخصائص اليونيكود، بنية التحكم `try/catch`، استخدام `@_` داخل توقيعات الإجراءات الفرعية، مساحة الاسم المضمنة، معدِّل كتلة `defer`، حدود مزدوجة إضافية للمُعاملات الشبيهة بالاقتباس، المُعاملات `any` و `all` لمعالجة القوائم.
الميزات المقبولة
دعم 64 بت، `die` يقبل مرجعًا، وحدة DB، مراجع ضعيفة، ترميز الملفات الداخلي، محاكاة `fork()`، `-Dusemultiplicity -Duseithreads`، دعم الأعداد العشرية الطويلة، فئة المحرف `\N` في التعبيرات النمطية، `(?{code})` و `(??{ code })`، مقابس نطاق Unix المجردة لنظام Linux، إجراءات Lvalue، أفعال التحكم في التراجع، طبقة الوصف `\x{FFFD}` للمُعاملات IO، `\s` في مطابقة التعبيرات النمطية للجدول العمودي، صيغة إلغاء المرجع اللاحق، إجراءات معجمية، عوامل التشغيل البيتية الخاصة بالسلاسل والأرقام، تأكيدات أبجدية، تشغيل البرامج النصية، المُعامل `isa` البيني، توقيعات الإجراءات الفرعية، عمليات المجموعات للتعبيرات النمطية، بنية التحكم `try/catch`، سمة `const`، حلقة `for` مع متغيرات تكرار متعددة.
الميزات التي تمت إزالتها
الخيوط بأسلوب 5.005، perlcc، نوع بيانات التجزئة الزائفة، خيارات GetOpt::Long يمكنها الآن أخذ قيم متعددة في وقت واحد (تجريبي)، التأكيدات، Test::Harness::Straps، `legacy`، `$_` المعجمي، تقبل دوال المصفوفات والهاش مراجع، `our` يمكن أن يكون له سمة اختيارية تجريبية `unique`، طبقة الوصف IO `:win32`.
الميزات التي تم التخلي عنها في مكانها
المطابقة الذكية (`~~`)، التبديل (`given/when`).

البناء
التغييرات
أغسطس 2015، النقل إلى Perl 5.22، إضافة معالجة NIL: إلى **afstat()**، إصلاح وراثة متغيرات البيئة بواسطة العمليات الفرعية، إصلاح `exec` و `exit` في العمليات الفرعية "المتفرعة"، إصلاح مشكلة في newlib unlink، والتي يمكن أن تسبب حلقات لا نهائية، إضافة محاكاة **flock()** باستخدام IDOS->LockRecord بفضل Tony Cook للاقتراح، إصلاح مشكلة حيث كان `kill` يستخدم نوعًا خاطئًا من معرفات العمليات. 27 نوفمبر 2013، إنشاء نظام تثبيت جديد يعتمد على روابط installperl وبتات حماية Amiga التي تم تعيينها بشكل صحيح الآن، Pod الآن افتراضي للنص، يجب أن يتعرف File::Spec الآن على مسار مطلق بأسلوب Amiga بالإضافة إلى مسار بأسلوب Unix. يجب أن تكون المسارات النسبية دائمًا بأسلوب Unix. 20 نوفمبر 2013، تم التكوين لاستخدام SDK:Local/C/perl لبدء البرامج النصية القياسية، تمت إضافة وحدة Amiga::Exec مع دعم لـ **Wait()** وأرقام إشارات AmigaOS. 10 أكتوبر 2013.

It takes an XS file (a superset of the C language with some Perl-specific extensions) and generates C code. This C code can then be compiled into a Perl extension module. =head1 EXPORT None. =head1 METHODS =head2 $pxs->new( %args ) Constructor for ExtUtils::ParseXS. Accepts the following arguments: =over =item C++ If set to true, C++ parsing is enabled. This means that C++ syntax, like C++ comments (//) and keywords (like class, template, etc.) are recognized. =item hiertype A string specifying the hierarchy of types. Default is 'Perl'. =item except If set to true, exceptions will be used for error handling. =item typemap A string or an arrayref of strings specifying the typemaps to use. These typemaps map Perl types to C types. =item prototypes If set to true, prototypes will be checked. =item versioncheck If set to true, the version of the extension will be checked. =item linenumbers If set to true, line numbers will be included in the generated C code for debugging purposes. =item optimize If set to true, optimization techniques will be applied to the generated C code. =item inout If set to true, input and output type checking will be performed. =item argtypes If set to true, argument types will be checked. =item s A string representing the XS code to be parsed. If not provided, the parser will read from STDIN. =item die_on_error If set to true, the parser will call C die() on error. =back =head2 $pxs->process_file( filename ) Processes the specified XS file. =head2 $pxs->report_error_count() Returns the number of errors encountered during parsing. =head1 AUTHOR Keith Conway =head1 COPYRIGHT Copyright (c) 2002-2004, Keith Conway, Society of Perl Programmers. This program is free software; you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the same terms as Perl itself, either Perl version 5.8.4 or, at your option, any later version of Perl 5 you may have available. =head1 SEE ALSO ExtUtils::Typemaps, ExtUtils::ParseXS::Constants, ExtUtils::ParseXS::Eval, ExtUtils::ParseXS::Node, ExtUtils::ParseXS::Utilities =cut */ /* =head1 NAME ExtUtils::ParseXS::Constants - Initialization values for some globals =head1 SYNOPSIS use ExtUtils::ParseXS::Constants; =head1 DESCRIPTION This module provides initialization values for some global variables used by ExtUtils::ParseXS. It is not intended to be used directly by users. =cut */ /* =head1 NAME ExtUtils::ParseXS::Eval - Clean package to evaluate code in =head1 SYNOPSIS use ExtUtils::ParseXS::Eval; =head1 SUBROUTINES =head2 $pxs->eval_output_typemap_code($typemapcode, $other_hashref) Evaluates the given typemap code in a clean package. =head2 $pxs->eval_input_typemap_code($typemapcode, $other_hashref) Evaluates the given typemap code in a clean package. =head1 TODO =cut */ /* =head1 NAME ExtUtils::ParseXS::Node - Classes for nodes of an ExtUtils::ParseXS AST =head1 SYNOPSIS use ExtUtils::ParseXS::Node; =head1 DESCRIPTION This module defines the classes used to represent the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) generated by ExtUtils::ParseXS. These classes are primarily for internal use by ExtUtils::ParseXS. =cut */ /* =head1 NAME ExtUtils::ParseXS::Utilities - Subroutines used with ExtUtils::ParseXS =head1 SYNOPSIS use ExtUtils::ParseXS::Utilities; =head1 SUBROUTINES =head2 standard_typemap_locations() =over =item Purpose Returns a list of standard locations where typemap files can be found. =item Arguments None. =item Return Value An array reference of strings, where each string is a path to a typemap directory. =back =head2 trim_whitespace() =over =item Purpose Removes leading and trailing whitespace from a string. =item Argument A string. =item Return Value The string with leading and trailing whitespace removed. =back =head2 C_string() =over =item Purpose Converts a Perl string into a C string literal, escaping special characters as necessary. =item Arguments =over =item * A Perl string. =item * An optional boolean indicating whether to include surrounding double quotes. =back =item Return Value A C string literal. =back =head2 valid_proto_string() =over =item Purpose Checks if a given string is a valid C function prototype. =item Arguments =over =item * A string representing the prototype. =back =item Return Value A boolean indicating whether the prototype is valid. =back =head2 process_typemaps() =over =item Purpose Processes a list of typemaps, merging them into a single typemap structure. =item Arguments =over =item * A reference to a typemap object. =item * An array reference of typemap file paths or strings. =back =item Return Value None. =back =head2 "map_type($self, $type, $varname)" Internal method to map a Perl type to its corresponding C type. =head2 standard_XS_defs() =over =item Purpose Returns a list of standard definitions used in XS files. =item Arguments None. =item Return Value An array reference of strings, where each string is a C preprocessor definition. =back =head2 analyze_preprocessor_statement() =over =item Purpose Analyzes a preprocessor statement (e.g., #ifdef, #ifndef, #if). =item Arguments =over =item * The preprocessor statement string. =back =back =head2 set_cond() =over =item Purpose Sets the condition for a preprocessor directive. =item Arguments =over =item * The condition string. =back =item Return Value None. =back =head2 current_line_number() =over =item Purpose Returns the current line number in the XS file being parsed. =item Arguments None. =item Return Value An integer representing the current line number. =back =head2 Error handling methods =over =item $self->Warn(@messages) Issues a warning message. =item $self->blurt(@messages) Issues a warning message and exits. =item $self->death(@messages) Exits with an error message. =item $self->WarnHint(@messages, $hints) Issues a warning message with hints. =back =head2 check_conditional_preprocessor_statements() =over =item Purpose Checks conditional preprocessor statements in the XS code. =item Arguments None. =item Return Value None. =back =head2 escape_file_for_line_directive() =over =item Purpose Escapes a filename so it can be used in a #line directive. =item Arguments =over =item * The filename string. =back =item Return Value The escaped filename string. =back =head2 report_typemap_failure =over =item Purpose Reports a failure to process a typemap. =item Arguments =over =item * The typemap name. =item * The error message. =back =item Return Value None. =back =cut */ /* =head1 NAME ExtUtils::Typemaps - Read/Write/Modify Perl/XS typemap files =head1 SYNOPSIS use ExtUtils::Typemaps; my $typemaps = ExtUtils::Typemaps->new(); $typemaps->add_typemap( 'typemap.txt' ); my $c_code = $typemaps->as_string(); =head1 DESCRIPTION This module provides functionality to read, write, and modify Perl/XS typemap files. Typemaps are used to map between Perl data types and C data types, enabling seamless interaction between Perl and C code. =head1 METHODS =head2 new() Constructor. Creates a new ExtUtils::Typemaps object. =head2 file() Sets or gets the filename associated with the typemaps. =head2 add_typemap() Adds a typemap from a file or a string. =head2 add_inputmap() Adds an input map entry. =head2 add_outputmap() Adds an output map entry. =head2 add_string() Adds a typemap entry from a string. =head2 remove_typemap() Removes a typemap entry. =head2 remove_inputmap() Removes an input map entry. =head2 remove_outputmap() Removes an output map entry. =head2 get_typemap() Retrieves a typemap entry. =head2 get_inputmap() Retrieves an input map entry. =head2 get_outputmap() Retrieves an output map entry. =head2 write() Writes the typemaps to a file. =head2 as_string() Returns the typemaps as a string. =head2 as_embedded_typemap() Returns the typemaps in a format suitable for embedding in C code. =head2 merge() Merges another typemap object into this one. =head2 is_empty() Checks if the typemap object is empty. =head2 list_mapped_ctypes() Lists all C types that are mapped. =head2 _get_typemap_hash() Internal method to get the typemap hash. =head2 _get_inputmap_hash() Internal method to get the input map hash. =head2 _get_outputmap_hash() Internal method to get the output map hash. =head2 _get_prototype_hash() Internal method to get the prototype hash. =head2 clone() Creates a deep copy of the typemap object. =head2 tidy_type() Cleans up and standardizes a type string. =head1 CAVEATS =head1 SEE ALSO ExtUtils::ParseXS, ExtUtils::Typemaps::Cmd =head1 AUTHOR Autrijus De =head1 COPYRIGHT & LICENSE =cut */ /* =head1 NAME ExtUtils::Typemaps::Cmd - Quick commands for handling typemaps =head1 SYNOPSIS use ExtUtils::Typemaps::Cmd qw(embeddable_typemap); my $typemap_string = embeddable_typemap('my_typemap.txt'); =head1 DESCRIPTION This module provides command-line utilities for handling typemap files. It is primarily intended for use within other tools and scripts. =head1 EXPORTED FUNCTIONS =head2 embeddable_typemap() =over =item Purpose Converts a typemap file into a string that can be embedded in C code. =item Arguments =over =item * A path to a typemap file. =back =back =head1 SEE ALSO ExtUtils::Typemaps =head1 AUTHOR Autrijus De =head1 COPYRIGHT & LICENSE =cut */ /* =head1 NAME ExtUtils::Typemaps::InputMap - Entry in the INPUT section of a typemap =head1 SYNOPSIS use ExtUtils::Typemaps::InputMap; my $input_map = ExtUtils::Typemaps::InputMap->new( xstype => 'SV*', code => '$sv', ); =head1 DESCRIPTION Represents an entry in the INPUT section of a typemap file. This defines how a C type is converted from a Perl value. =head1 METHODS =head2 new() Constructor. =head2 code() Gets or sets the C code snippet for the input conversion. =head2 xstype() Gets or sets the XS type associated with this input map. =head2 cleaned_code() Returns the C code snippet, with any surrounding whitespace removed. =head1 SEE ALSO ExtUtils::Typemaps, ExtUtils::Typemaps::OutputMap =head1 AUTHOR Autrijus De =head1 COPYRIGHT & LICENSE =cut */ /* =head1 NAME ExtUtils::Typemaps::OutputMap - Entry in the OUTPUT section of a typemap =head1 SYNOPSIS use ExtUtils::Typemaps::OutputMap; my $output_map = ExtUtils::Typemaps::OutputMap->new( xstype => 'SV*', code => '$sv', ); =head1 DESCRIPTION Represents an entry in the OUTPUT section of a typemap file. This defines how a Perl value is converted from a C type. =head1 METHODS =head2 new() Constructor. =head2 code() Gets or sets the C code snippet for the output conversion. =head2 xstype() Gets or sets the XS type associated with this output map. =head1 */

    NAME

    Locale::Maketext::Lexicon - Base class for Locale::Maketext lexicons

    SYNOPSIS

        use Locale::Maketext::Lexicon;
    my $lex = Locale::Maketext::Lexicon->new(...);
    # ...

    DESCRIPTION

    This is the base class for all lexicons in the Locale::Maketext module hierarchy.

    Lexicons are the core of Locale::Maketext. They provide the translation lookups, pluralization rules, number formatting, and other language-specific behaviors.

    You will usually not use this class directly, but rather use one of the specialized lexicon classes like:

    Locale::Maketext::Lexicon::Gettext
    Uses the standard gettext PO/POT/MO files for translations.
    Locale::Maketext::Lexicon::Simple
    Uses simple text files for translations (less features, but simpler to use).
    Locale::Maketext::Lexicon::Shell
    Translates by invoking external commands (e.g. for gettext).

    The primary interface to lexicons is through the Locale::Maketext class itself.

    METHODS

    Lexicon objects are created using the new() method. The arguments depend on the specific lexicon class.

    This class provides default implementations for methods that are common to all lexicons. Specific lexicon classes may override these methods to provide language-specific behavior.

    add_languages()
    Adds new languages to the lexicon. Typically called by the Locale::Maketext object.
    get_languages()
    Returns a list of languages supported by this lexicon.
    languages()
    Returns a list of languages currently loaded by this lexicon.
    make_locale()
    Creates a new Locale::Maketext object for a specific language and country code.
    gettext()
    Translates a string.
    ngettext()
    Translates a string, handling plural forms.
    quant()
    Formats a number with a singular and optional plural form.
    numf()
    Formats a number according to locale-specific conventions.
    numerate()
    Similar to quant() but with more options for handling negative numbers.
    sprintf()
    Performs locale-aware string formatting, similar to Perl's sprintf.
    language_tag()
    Returns the BCP 47 language tag for the current language.
    encoding()
    Returns the character encoding used by this lexicon.
    blacklist()
    Adds a list of languages to the blacklist, preventing them from being used.
    allowlist()
    Adds a list of languages to the allowlist, ensuring only these languages are used.
    whitelist()
    An alias for allowlist().

    UTILITY METHODS

    These methods provide helper functions for language-related tasks.

    quant($number, $singular)
    Selects the correct string for a given number, using only the singular form if the number is not 1.
    quant($number, $singular, $plural)
    Selects the correct string for a given number, using the appropriate singular or plural form.
    quant($number, $singular, $plural, $negative)
    Selects the correct string for a given number, considering singular, plural, and a specific string for negative numbers.
    numf($number)
    Formats a number according to locale-specific conventions (e.g., thousands separators, decimal points).
    numerate($number, $singular, $plural, $negative)
    Similar to quant(), but provides more fine-grained control over number formatting and pluralization, especially for negative numbers.
    sprintf($format, @items)
    Performs locale-aware string formatting. Placeholders in the $format string are replaced by the corresponding items in @items, respecting locale-specific conventions for numbers, dates, etc.
    language_tag()
    Returns the BCP 47 language tag (e.g., "en-US", "fr") for the current language setting of the lexicon.
    encoding()
    Returns the character encoding (e.g., "UTF-8") that the lexicon uses.

    Memoize - Make functions faster by trading space for time

    SYNOPSIS
    DESCRIPTION
    EXAMPLE
    DETAILS

    Memoize

    NAME
    Memoize - A framework for memoizing subroutine results.
    VERSION
    1.00
    SYNOPSIS
    use Memoize;

# Memoize a subroutine.
memoize 'function_name';

# Memoize a subroutine with a specific cache.
memoize 'function_name', &MyCache;

# Memoize a subroutine with options.
memoize 'function_name',
    $cache_size => 100,
    $file_name => '/tmp/mycache',
    $compress_level => 9,
    $null_entry => undef;

# Memoize a subroutine that takes arguments.
memoize 'function_name', \&arg_hash_foo;

# Unmemoize a subroutine.
unmemoize 'function_name';

# Flush a memoized subroutine's cache.
flush_cache 'function_name';

# Check if a subroutine is memoized.
is_memoized('function_name');

# Retrieve the cache used by a subroutine.
cache_get('function_name');

# Set cache for a subroutine.
cache_set(\&foo, MyCache->new( ... ));

# Memoize a subroutine with custom key generation.
memoize 'function_name', \&make_key;
    DESCRIPTION
    This module provides a framework for memoizing subroutine results. Memoization is a form of caching where the results of expensive function calls are cached and returned when the same inputs occur again. This can significantly speed up programs that call the same functions with the same arguments repeatedly.
    DETAILS
    OPTIONS
    INSTALL
    NORMALIZER
    "SCALAR_CACHE", "LIST_CACHE"
    "MEMORY", "HASH", "TIE", "FAULT", "MERGE"
    OTHER FACILITIES

    "flush_cache"

    SYNOPSIS
    DESCRIPTION

    SYNOPSIS

    use Net::FTP;

    my $ftp = Net::FTP->new("ftp.example.com", Debug => 0);

    my $success = $ftp->login('myusername', 'mypassword');

    my @files = $ftp->nlst();

    $ftp->quit;

    DESCRIPTION

    This module implements the FTP client protocol. It is designed to be as easy to use as possible.

    The following methods are available:

    new([$host][, %options])

    Constructs a new Net::FTP object. If $host is given, it attempts to connect to that host. Otherwise, you must connect later using the connect() method.

    The following options are accepted:

    Debug
    If true, causes the FTP commands and responses to be printed to STDOUT.
    Timeout
    Specifies a timeout for blocking network operations. Defaults to 120 seconds.
    Firewall
    If true, causes the use of the firewall protocol.
    FirewallType
    If set to "SOCKS", causes the use of SOCKS firewall protocol. You must have the Net::SOCKS module installed.
    connect($host)

    Connects to the specified host. This is only needed if you didn't supply a host to new().

    login([$login[, $password[, $account]]])

    Logs into the FTP server. If no arguments are provided, it will prompt for username, password, and account.

    starttls()

    Attempts to start TLS (Transport Layer Security) encryption on the control connection. You must have the IO::Socket::SSL module installed.

    stoptls()

    Shuts down TLS encryption on the control connection.

    prot($level)

    Sets the protection level for data connections. $level can be 'C' (clear) or 'P' (private). Defaults to 'C'.

    host()

    Returns the hostname of the current connection.

    account($acct)

    Sets the FTP account. This is only needed for some servers.

    authorize([$auth[, $resp]])

    Sends an AUTH command with the given argument. If $resp is provided, it checks if the server's response matches.

    site($args)

    Sends SITE command with the given arguments.

    ascii()

    Sets the transfer type to ASCII.

    binary()

    Sets the transfer type to Binary.

    type([$type])

    Sets the transfer type. $type can be 'a' for ASCII or 'i' for binary. If no argument is given, it returns the current type.

    rename($oldname, $newname)

    Renames a file on the server.

    delete($filename)

    Deletes a file on the server.

    cwd([$dir])

    Changes the current directory on the server. If no argument is given, it changes to the home directory.

    cdup()

    Changes the current directory to the parent directory.

    passive([$passive])

    Sets the passive mode. If $passive is true, passive mode is enabled. If false, active mode is enabled. If no argument is given, it returns the current setting.

    pwd()

    Returns the current working directory on the server.

    restart($where)

    Restarts a file transfer at a specific offset.

    rmdir($dir[, $recurse])

    Removes a directory on the server. If $recurse is true, it will attempt to remove the directory and all its contents.

    mkdir($dir[, $recurse])

    Creates a directory on the server. If $recurse is true, it will attempt to create parent directories as needed.

    alloc($size[, $record_size])

    Allocates space on the server for a file.

    ls([$dir])

    Returns a list of files in the specified directory. If no directory is given, it lists the current directory.

    dir([$dir])

    Returns a detailed listing of files in the specified directory. If no directory is given, it lists the current directory.

    get($remote_file[, $local_file[, $where]])

    Retrieves a file from the server. If $local_file is not specified, the file is saved with the same name in the current directory. If $where is specified, it is used as the restart offset.

    put($local_file[, $remote_file])

    Uploads a file to the server. If $remote_file is not specified, the file is uploaded with the same name.

    put_unique($local_file[, $remote_file])

    Uploads a file to the server and gives it a unique name.

    append($local_file[, $remote_file])

    Appends a local file to a remote file on the server.

    unique_name()

    Returns a unique filename that can be used on the server.

    mdtm($file)

    Returns the modification time of a file on the server.

    size($file)

    Returns the size of a file on the server.

    supported($cmd)

    Checks if the server supports a given FTP command.

    hash([$filehandle_glob_ref[, $bytes_per_hash_mark]])

    Turns on or off the hash mark printing. If $filehandle_glob_ref is provided, it will print a hash mark for every $bytes_per_hash_mark bytes transferred.

    feature($name)

    Requests a server-specific feature.

    nlst([$dir])

    Returns a list of filenames in the specified directory. If no directory is given, it lists the current directory.

    list([$dir])

    Returns a detailed listing of files in the specified directory. If no directory is given, it lists the current directory.

    retr($file)

    Retrieves a file from the server.

    stor($file)

    Stores a file on the server.

    stou($file)

    Stores a unique file on the server.

    appe($file)

    Appends a file to a remote file on the server.

    port([$port])

    Sets the server port for active mode data connections.

    eprt([$port])

    Sets the server port for extended active mode data connections.

    pasv()

    Enables passive mode.

    epsv()

    Enables extended passive mode.

    pasv_xfer($src_file, $dest_server[, $dest_file ])

    Transfers a file from the current server to another server using passive mode.

    pasv_xfer_unique($src_file, $dest_server[, $dest_file ])

    Transfers a file from the current server to another server using passive mode and gives it a unique name.

    pasv_wait($non_pasv_server)

    Waits for a non-passive data connection to be established.

    abort()

    Aborts a file transfer.

    quit()

    Quits the FTP session.

    كيف أقوم بنقل الملفات في الوضع الثنائي؟
    كيف يمكنني الحصول على حجم ملف على خادم FTP بعيد؟
    كيف يمكنني الحصول على وقت تعديل ملف على خادم FTP بعيد؟
    كيف يمكنني تغيير أذونات ملف على خادم بعيد؟
    هل يمكنني إجراء عملية إعادة تنزيل مثل أمر ftp؟
    كيف يمكنني الحصول على قائمة دليل من خادم FTP؟
    تغيير الدليل إلى "" لا يفشل؟
    أنا خلف جدار حماية SOCKS، ولكن خيار Firewall لا يعمل؟
    أنا خلف جدار حماية بروكسي FTP، ولكن لا يمكنني الوصول إلى الأجهزة الخارجية؟
    جدار حماية بروكسي FTP الخاص بي لا يستمع على المنفذ 21
    هل من الممكن تغيير أذونات الملف على خادم FTP؟
    لقد رأيت نصوصًا تستدعي وظيفة تسمى message، ولكن لا يمكنني العثور عليها موثقة؟
    لماذا لا تنفذ Net::FTP طرق mput و mget؟
    استخدام Net::SMTP
    لماذا لا يمكن استخدام الجزء من عنوان البريد الإلكتروني بعد @ كاسم المضيف؟
    لماذا لا تقوم Net::SMTP بإجراء عمليات بحث DNS MX؟
    الوظيفة verify تعيد دائمًا true؟
    تصحيح أخطاء النصوص
    كيف يمكنني تصحيح أخطاء نصوصي التي تستخدم وحدات Net::*؟
    المؤلف وحقوق النشر

    Pod::Checker - التحقق من وثائق pod بحثًا عن أخطاء في بناء الجملة

    الملخص
    الخيارات/الوسائط
    podchecker()
    -warnings => val, -quiet => val
    الوصف
    التشخيصات
    الأخطاء
    عنوان فارغ، =over في السطر N بدون =back مغلق، لقد نسيت '=back' قبل '=headN'، =over هو آخر شيء في المستند؟!، =item خارج أي =over، =back بدون =over، لا يمكن أن يكون هناك 0 في =over N، يجب أن يكون =over: '=over' أو '=over رقم موجب'، =begin TARGET بدون =end TARGET مطابق، =begin بدون هدف؟، =end TARGET بدون =begin مطابق، '=end' بدون هدف؟، '=end TARGET' غير صالح، =end CONTENT لا يتطابق مع =begin TARGET، =for بدون هدف؟، رابط داخلي غير محلول NAME، توجيه غير معروف: CMD، حذف رمز تنسيق غير معروف SEQ، تسلسل SEQ<> غير منتهٍ، E<...> يحيط بمحتوى غريب، E<> فارغ، "L<>" فارغ، X<> فارغ، نص سبوري بعد =pod / =cut، =back لا يأخذ أي وسائط، ولكنك قلت =back ARGUMENT، لا ينبغي أن تكون توجيهات =pod أطول من سطر واحد! تجاهل جميع سطور المحتوى N، تم العثور على =cut خارج كتلة pod، صيغة =encoding غير صالحة: CONTENT
    تحذيرات
    أوامر متداخلة CMD<...CMD<...>...>، تكرارات متعددة (N) للهدف name، سطر يحتوي على مسافات بيضاء فقط في فقرة، =item ليس له محتويات، لا يمكنك الحصول على =items (كما في السطر N) إلا إذا كان أول شيء بعد =over هو =item، متوقع '=item EXPECTED VALUE'، متوقع '=item *'، تطابق محتمل لنوع =item: تم العثور على 'x' يقود تعريفًا مفترضًا =item، لديك '=item x' بدلاً من '=item N' المتوقع، محتوى E غير معروف في E<CONTENT>، كتلة =over/=back فارغة، قسم فارغ في الفقرة السابقة، فقرة حرفية في قسم NAME، =headn بدون مستوى أعلى سابق، Z<> غير فارغ
    الروابط التشعبية
    تجاهل المسافات البيضاء البادئة/اللاحقة في الرابط، نص بديل/عقدة '%s' تحتوي على | أو / غير مُفلت

    ملخص
    الوصف
    Call Pod::Perldoc::GetOptsOO::getopts($object, \@ARGV, $truth), Given -n, if there's a opt_n_with, it'll call $object->opt_n_with( ARGUMENT ) (e.g., "-n foo" => $object->opt_n_with('foo'). Ditto "-nfoo"), Otherwise (given -n) if there's an opt_n, we'll call it $object->opt_n($truth) (Truth defaults to 1), Otherwise we try calling $object->handle_unknown_option('n') (and we increment the error count by the return value of it), If there's no handle_unknown_option, then we just warn, and then increment the error counter

    TAP::Parser::Scheduler - Schedule tests during parallel testing

    VERSION
    SYNOPSIS
    DESCRIPTION
    METHODS
    Class Methods
    Rules data structure
    By default, all tests are eligible to be run in parallel. Specifying any of your own rules removes this one, "First match wins". The first rule that matches a test will be the one that applies, Any test which does not match a rule will be run in sequence at the end of the run, The existence of a rule does not imply selecting a test. You must still specify the tests to run, Specifying a rule to allow tests to run in parallel does not make the run in parallel. You still need specify the number of parallel "jobs" in your Harness object

    Test2 - إطار عمل لكتابة أدوات اختبار تعمل معًا.

    الوصف
    ما الجديد؟
    أسهل في اختبار أدوات الاختبار الجديدة، قدرات تشخيص أفضل، يعتمد على الأحداث، واجهة برمجة تطبيقات أكثر اكتمالاً، دعم للمخرجات بخلاف TAP، تطبيق اختبار فرعي أكثر منطقية، دعم للترابط/التفرع
    البدء

    Test2، يصف هذا تخطيط مساحة الأسماء لنظام Test2 البيئي. ليست كل مساحات الأسماء المدرجة هنا جزءًا من توزيع Test2، وبعضها مطبق في Test2::Suite.

    Test2::Formatter - Namespace for formatters.

    DESCRIPTION
    This namespace contains different formatter classes that can be used to render test results in various formats. Formatters are responsible for converting test events into human-readable output or machine-parseable data.
    CREATING FORMATTERS
    When creating a custom formatter, you will typically need to implement several methods to handle different types of test events. Key information you might need to track includes: The number of tests that were planned, The number of tests actually seen, The number of tests which failed, A boolean indicating whether or not the test suite passed, A boolean indicating whether or not this call is for a subtest
    SOURCE

    Test2::Formatter::TAP - Standard TAP formatter

    DESCRIPTION
    This formatter implements the Test Anything Protocol (TAP) standard. It is used to output test results in a format that can be easily parsed by TAP-compliant test harness tools.
    SYNOPSIS
    use Test2::Formatter::TAP;

my $tap = Test2::Formatter::TAP->new;
# ... use $tap to format events ...
    METHODS
    no_numbers
    Get or set whether line numbers should be included in the TAP output. $bool = $tap->no_numbers, $tap->set_no_numbers($bool)
    handles
    Get or set the filehandles to write TAP output to. $arrayref = $tap->handles, $tap->set_handles(\@handles)
    encoding
    Get or set the output encoding. $encoding = $tap->encoding, $tap->encoding($encoding)
    write
    Write a test event to the output. $tap->write($e, $num)
    SOURCE
    MAINTAINERS
    Chad Granum <exodist@cpan.org>
    AUTHORS
    Chad Granum <exodist@cpan.org>, Kent Fredric <kentnl@cpan.org>
    COPYRIGHT

    Test2::Hub - The conduit through which all events flow.

    SYNOPSIS
    use Test2::Hub;

my $hub = Test2::Hub->new;
# ... use $hub to manage test events ...
    DESCRIPTION
    The Test2::Hub is the central component for managing test events. It acts as a dispatch mechanism, receiving test events and routing them to various listeners, formatters, and filters. It also keeps track of the overall test state.
    COMMON TASKS
    SENDING EVENTS
    Events are sent to the hub using the `send` or `process` methods.
    ALTERING OR REMOVING EVENTS
    Filters can be added to modify or discard events before they are processed further.
    LISTENING FOR EVENTS
    Callbacks can be registered to react to specific events using `listen`.
    POST-TEST BEHAVIORS
    The hub manages the state of the test run, including pass/fail status and planned tests.
    SETTING THE FORMATTER
    A formatter can be associated with the hub to control the output format.
    METHODS
    send
    Send an event to the hub. $hub->send($event)
    process
    Process an event. $hub->process($event)
    format
    Set the formatter for the hub. Returns the previous formatter. $old = $hub->format($formatter)
    listen
    Register a callback to listen for events. $sub = $hub->listen(sub { ... }, %optional_params)
    unlisten
    Remove a previously registered listener. $hub->unlisten($sub)
    filter
    Register a filter to modify or discard events. $sub = $hub->filter(sub { ... }, %optional_params)
    pre_filter
    Register a filter that runs before other filters. $sub = $hub->pre_filter(sub { ... }, %optional_params)
    unfilter
    Remove a previously registered filter. $hub->unfilter($sub)
    pre_unfilter
    Remove a previously registered pre-filter. $hub->pre_unfilter($sub)
    follow_op
    Register a callback to follow operations. $hub->follow_op(sub { ... })
    add_context_acquire
    Add a callback for acquiring context. $sub = $hub->add_context_acquire(sub { ... })
    remove_context_acquire
    Remove a context acquisition callback. $hub->remove_context_acquire($sub)
    add_context_init
    Add a callback for initializing context. $sub = $hub->add_context_init(sub { ... })
    remove_context_init
    Remove a context initialization callback. $hub->remove_context_init($sub)
    add_context_release
    Add a callback for releasing context. $sub = $hub->add_context_release(sub { ... })
    remove_context_release
    Remove a context release callback. $hub->remove_context_release($sub)
    cull
    Clean up the hub. $hub->cull()
    pid
    Get the current process ID. $pid = $hub->pid()
    tid
    Get the current thread ID. $tid = $hub->tid()
    hid
    Get the hub ID. $hud = $hub->hid()
    uuid
    Get the hub UUID. $uuid = $hub->uuid()
    ipc
    Get the IPC object associated with the hub. $ipc = $hub->ipc()
    set_no_ending
    Set whether to prevent the hub from automatically ending the test run. $hub->set_no_ending($bool)
    no_ending
    Check if the hub is prevented from automatically ending the test run. $bool = $hub->no_ending
    active
    Check if the hub is currently active. $bool = $hub->active
    set_active
    Set the active state of the hub. $hub->set_active($bool)
    STATE METHODS
    reset_state
    Reset the internal state of the hub. $hub->reset_state()
    count
    Get the total number of tests seen. $num = $hub->count
    failed
    Get the number of failed tests. $num = $hub->failed
    ended
    Check if the test run has ended. $bool = $hub->ended
    is_passing
    Check if the test run is currently passing. $bool = $hub->is_passing
    is_passing
    Set the passing status of the test run. $hub->is_passing($bool)
    plan
    Set or get the test plan. $hub->plan($plan), $plan = $hub->plan
    check_plan
    Check if the number of tests seen matches the plan. $bool = $hub->check_plan
    THIRD PARTY META-DATA
    The hub can be extended to handle third-party meta-data.
    SOURCE
    MAINTAINERS
    Chad Granum <exodist@cpan.org>
    AUTHORS
    Chad Granum <exodist@cpan.org>
    COPYRIGHT

    SYNOPSIS
    use Test2::IPC;

# Enable IPC
Test2::IPC->enable;

# ... run tests ...

# Optionally disable IPC
Test2::IPC->disable;
    DESCRIPTION
    This module provides support for Inter-Process Communication (IPC), which is necessary for running tests in a threaded or forked environment. It allows test results to be communicated between different processes.
    DISABLING IT
    You can disable IPC support using the `disable` method.
    EXPORTS
    The following functions are exported by default: cull()
    SOURCE
    MAINTAINERS
    Chad Granum <exodist@cpan.org>
    AUTHORS
    Chad Granum <exodist@cpan.org>
    COPYRIGHT

    Test2::Plugin - Base class for Test2 plugins.

    DESCRIPTION
    This is the base class for all Test2 plugins. Plugins extend the functionality of Test2 by providing custom behaviors or integrations.
    CREATING PLUGINS
    To create a plugin, inherit from Test2::Plugin and implement the desired methods. Plugins can hook into various stages of the testing process.
    SOURCE
    MAINTAINERS
    Chad Granum <exodist@cpan.org>
    AUTHORS

    Test2::Require - Module for conditional testing.

    DESCRIPTION
    This module provides functionality for conditionally running tests based on certain requirements, such as the availability of modules or specific system conditions.
    SYNOPSIS
    use Test2::Require qw(require_module);

# Require a module, skip tests if not available
require_module('Some::Module') or plan skip_all => 'Cannot test without Some::Module';

# ... tests that depend on Some::Module ...
    FUNCTIONS
    require_module
    Attempts to require a module. Returns true on success, false on failure. Can be used with `plan skip_all` to skip tests if the module is not found.
    SOURCE
    MAINTAINERS
    Chad Granum <exodist@cpan.org>
    AUTHORS
    Chad Granum <exodist@cpan.org>
    COPYRIGHT

    Test2::V0 - Convenience wrapper for common testing tasks.

    DESCRIPTION
    Test2::V0 provides a simplified interface for common testing operations, making it easier to write tests quickly. It often involves pre-configuring a hub and formatter.
    SYNOPSIS
    use Test2::V0;

pass("This test passed");
ok(1, "This condition is true");
diag("Some diagnostic information");
    FUNCTIONS
    Test2::V0 exports a variety of functions for common testing tasks, including: pass, fail, ok, not_ok, diag, note, bail_out, plan, skip_all, etc.
    SOURCE
    MAINTAINERS
    Chad Granum <exodist@cpan.org>
    AUTHORS
    Chad Granum <exodist@cpan.org>
    COPYRIGHT

    Test2::Refine - Refine test results.

    DESCRIPTION
    This module allows you to refine or modify test results after they have been generated. This can be useful for post-processing or adjusting test outcomes.
    SYNOPSIS
    use Test2::Refine;

# Get the current test hub
my $hub = Test2::Hub->current;

# Refine the results (example: modify a failure message)
Test2::Refine->refine($hub, sub {
    # ... logic to refine events ...
});
    METHODS
    refine
    Applies a refinement callback to the test events in a hub. Test2::Refine->refine($hub, $callback)

$buffer->print("Hello");

    الاسم
    Test2::Tools::Exports - أدوات للتحقق من صحة المصدرين
    الإصدار
    0.000001
    ملخص
    use Test2::Tools::Exports qw( imported_ok not_imported_ok );

my $loaded = Module::Runtime::require_module('Some::Module');

ok $loaded;

# will fail if Some::Module does not export 'function_a' or 'function_b'
ok imported_ok(qw( function_a function_b ));

# will fail if Some::Module exports 'function_c'
ok not_imported_ok(qw( function_c ));

# use for importing specific things
ok imported_ok('Some::Module', qw( function_a function_b ));
ok not_imported_ok('Some::Module', qw( function_c ));
    الوصف

    This module provides tools for validating that modules have exported what you expect them to.

    This is generally useful when you are testing a module that uses another module, and you want to ensure that the underlying module is exporting the correct symbols. Or for testing that a module does NOT export symbols it should not.

    التصدير

    No exports by default. To get them:

    use Test2::Tools::Exports qw( imported_ok not_imported_ok );
    المؤلفون
    Chad Granum <exodist@cpan.org>
    حقوق النشر
